reviews.rationale: Scott amendment3 replaces the specified Print119-1 text with a complete HEA foreign-gift/contract disclosure and compliance regime. It specifies $100,000 annual/$250,000 three-calendar-year reporting thresholds, annual July31 timing, foreign ownership/control reporting, records and true-copy/translation requirements, public-access and privacy limits, accuracy/cure and qualified enforcement, individual non-agent student-payment exclusions, research-risk exceptions, foundation coverage and rulemaking/effectiveness. Foreign-source citizenship and country fields identify covered funding/disclosures; reported restricted-gift conditions concerning student selection/admission do not themselves create a personal immigration-status or admission rule. The literal repeated purpose wording is preserved, not repaired. This is institutional financial transparency/compliance rather than human admission, immigration status, citizenship eligibility or a direct border mechanism. No broader parent-title prohibitions, donor guilt, present legal applicability or actual educational/security outcomes inferred. Initial own proceedings March25, resumed recorded rejection March27:199-214,23Not Voting. Initial question, voice result, recorded demand and postponement precede the separate resumed recorded order and outcome. No inferred motive, ideology, character, corruption, causality, endorsement or voting recommendation; no methodology change or publication.

Pettersen PartA3 gives the entire CMS August22,2024 SMD24-003 guidance for budget neutrality of section1115(a) Medicaid demonstrations the force and effect of law. The complete letter and dated1315(a) authority retain case-specific waiver/expenditure conditions; without-waiver/with-waiver limits, per-capita/aggregate methods, hypothetical limits, 3percent HRSN/15percent infrastructure boundaries, DSH diversion, savings rollovers, rebasing, monitoring/corrective plans and return of excess funds. These are expenditure-budget methods for approved demonstrations; the amendment does not create immigration-status, admission, citizenship or status-governed personal benefit eligibility. No repeal of other eligibility law, guaranteed waiver approval or actual health/cost effects inferred. Actual own June4 recorded vote tied213-213,12Not Voting, and was rejected. Carter en-bloc2 combines all seven Report167 amendments1/14/15/19/25/28/32 in one choice. Arrington1 adds $4.1million to the Air Force military-construction appropriation and separately its planning ceiling, reducing NATO Security Investment by $4.1million; the ceiling change is not a second $4.1million appropriation. Houchin14 reduces VBA general operating expenses by $5million and increases Medical Services by $5million. Five paired same-heading reductions/increases have zero net amount: unaccompanied housing $1million, Navy/Marine construction $1million, Medical Community Care $1million, Medical Services $1million and Army National Guard construction $55million. Whole actual target funding paragraphs/provisos and bounded NATO/veteran-support authority retained. Debate project descriptions and references to foreign nationals at bases do not add a binding project earmark or a personal immigration/admission/citizenship-status mechanism to those operative edits. Existing medical priorities and qualified authorities are context, not changed eligibility criteria. Actual initial composition/question and resumed219-206,13Not Voting agreement preserved. Complete $60million Iron Dome, $127million SRBMD, $40million qualified SRBMD co-production, $100million upper-tier/Arrow3 and $173million Arrow improvements suballocations retained with agreement/law conditions. Removing this earmark/directive is not an automatic $500million account-total reduction, a ban on all Israeli assistance or repeal of all defense programs.
